claim_boundary: one domain, one engine; nothing here establishes general recursive self-improvement
name: CIRCUIT1

questions.1 accumulation: held-out tasks solved by the last engine of `lineage` against `frozen`, same budget, paired by seed; and against `frozen` with 10 and 100 times the budget
questions.2 cumulative: held-out tasks solved by `lineage` against `together` (as many components, one step)
questions.4 yield: tasks gained on the learning set at each step of `lineage`, in order: does a later step gain more than an earlier one, and what ends the lineage
questions.5 improving the improver: for every procedure variant, learning tasks gained by its lineage on family set A and on family set B (mean over seeds). Is the variant that gains most on A better on B than the seed procedure, and what is the rank correlation of the variants between A and B

reading: differences are counts of tasks, reported per seed with their mean; five seeds support no significance claim beyond an exact sign test at 1/32. Whatever the outcome, the procedure variants are chosen by a fixed search written by hand: question 5 measures whether a better improver can be selected and carries over, not recursion
stopping_rule: a lineage ends at the first step that keeps no component, or at the generation limit
unit_of_compute: one component application in the search; identical budgets per task for every arm
